text:
alex_h: FYI vendor delivered a security assessment with 6 findings. One of them is about archival log access that they claim allows exfil via admin UI. attaching the PDF in #vendor-reports :link: @maria_g @devon_s please take a look

maria_g: thanks. which finding ID is that? and did they provide PoC steps?

alex_h: it's finding 3. short excerpt from their report:
```
Find3: 'Archive log retrieval via expired presign path + insufficient KMS policy bounds; attacker can download and decrypt archived logs from backup-bucket using admin-console flow.'
PoC (vendor): 1) obtain admin console token via SSO misconfig 2) call GET /internal/logs/archived?token=xyz 3) follow presigned redirect to s3 and run `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-backups/logs.tar.gz ./` 4) kms:Decrypt allowed for principal `svc:external-assessor`
```

devon_s: ok. does our backup-bucket actually allow presigned urls? we use server-side encryption with CMK for backups.

raman: I pulled the report and the repro steps. vendor's PoC assumes an SSO assertion can mint an admin-session for their test principal; we don't see that flow in our telemetry for their scan times. I did find a poorly-scoped KMS key policy on the backups CMK (key alias: alias/backup-logs-rw) that granted `kms:Decrypt` to a role ARN pattern that is broader than intended. snippet of the offending binding:
```
"Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-*"},
"Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
"Effect": "Allow"
```
This wildcard could let cross-account roles decrypt if they can assume an allowed role.

alex_h: hmm. vendor says it was high severity. do we agree? vendor's argument: decrypted PII in logs could be exfiltrated.

maria_g: impact makes sense, but we need to validate exploitability. If SSO can't mint admin tokens cross-account then step 1 fails.

raman: agreed. current assessment from infra/security: severity = MEDIUM. Rationale: fixable misconfig + requires privilege escalation (SSO/assertion). If vendor demonstrated admin access it's higher. We should ask for evidence of how they obtained the admin session.

sec-bot: New ticket created: SEC-2026 - "Investigation: Archive log access claim (vendor finding 3)" assigned to @raman, priority P2. https://tickets.company/SEC-2026

devon_s: i'll attempt a repro using a restricted test account. can someone drop me the exact object key and timestamps vendor used? also need an example presign flow if they included one.

alex_h: vendor used `s3://redwood-backups/2025-11-08/logs-archive-001.tar.gz` and timestamps around 2025-11-08T13:02Z in their PoC. they included this HTTP snippet:
```
GET /internal/logs/archive?archive_id=001&token=abc123 HTTP/1.1
Host: internal.redwood.local
Authorization: Bearer <admin-session-token>
```

maria_g: @raman can you also check our CloudTrail for any console-assume events tied to that time window? we need the chain.

raman: looking now. initial findings: no cross-account assume-role events at that timestamp. I do see one internal service account (svc-ops) assuming a role and then listing backups. svc-ops is in-account and supposed to have limited access. Policy on svc-ops allowed `s3:GetObject` on backups and the CMK policy allowed decrypt for `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-ops*`. That explains the presign+download path but not an external assessor. vendor may have used an in-house flow or simulated a stolen token.

devon_s: ok i'll try to reproduce locally with svc-ops but in a limited environment. steps I'll run:
1) assume-role `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-ops-runner`
2) call internal archiver endpoint with archive_id=001
3) follow redirect and attempt `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-backups/2025-11-08/logs-archive-001.tar.gz ./`
4) try `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://enc_blob --key-id alias/backup-logs-rw`

raman: note: before you decrypt, ensure you use a test copy. i'm rotating key policy to remove the wildcard principal. i'll push a policy update in 30m then we can validate change.

alex_h: please capture screenshots/console logs of any presigned url + HTTP response headers from internal archiver so we can hand those to vendor as evidence. vendor asked for auditable proof for retest.

maria_g: vendor's severity dispute: they marked high; we are proposing medium pending proof. we should draft a response template: 1) request full PoC (session tokens and steps) 2) offer retest after we patch policy 3) ask for CVSS justification.

raman: agreed. i'll apply a constrained CMK policy that explicitly lists allowed principals (no wildcard) and add a Condition requiring `aws:SourceAccount` for the kms:Decrypt statement. also i'll add an S3 bucket policy that denies `s3:GetObject` for requests without `x-amz-server-side-encryption` header for backup objects to be safe.

sec-bot: SEC-2026 updated: "CMK policy constrained, bucket deny added, pending vendor retest" P2 -> Note added by raman.

devon_s: reproduced download but could not decrypt because after my test keys were removed decrypt failed with `AccessDeniedException`. logs: `KMSAccessDenied: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abc123: caller is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt`

alex_h: that's good. can you attach those logs here and mark timestamps so we can show vendor the before/after?

devon_s: attaching short output (copied):
```
$ aws s3 cp s3://redwood-backups/2025-11-08/logs-archive-001.tar.gz ./
download: s3://.../logs-archive-001.tar.gz to ./logs-archive-001.tar.gz
$ aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://enc_blob --key-id alias/backup-logs-rw
An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Decrypt operation: Caller is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on key abc123
```

raman: perfect — that's the evidence we need. I'll notify vendor and request a retest. Suggest we propose severity -> MEDIUM in our response but invite them to argue with PoC showing admin session creation.

maria_g: fine with MEDIUM with that context. I'll draft the response and ping @legal for any disclosure wording.

alex_h: thanks all. next steps: raman to close the policy gap, devon to upload logs to SEC ticket, maria to send vendor reply template. we'll reconvene after vendor retest. :thumbsup:

raman: done. policy change PR: https://git.company/repo/infra/kms/PR-482 — applied to prod. will monitor for any errors.

sec-bot: SEC-2026 status: waiting on vendor retest.
